analyst.summary: PFC is India's largest state-backed power-sector lender, and its FY26 numbers look strong on the surface - record profit, sharply lower bad loans, and a large dividend. Looking closer, much of that improvement rests on the resolution of one big stressed thermal-power loan (KSK Mahanadi) rather than broad-based portfolio health, and the company still carries meaningful legacy stressed exposures and high borrowings relative to its own capital (typical for this kind of lender, but still a real risk if the power sector sees fresh stress). Growth is tilting toward renewable-energy financing - a genuine long-term tailwind - but actual loan disbursements were flat-to-down this year even as approved-but-undrawn loan sanctions stayed large. A major merger with sister company REC is in motion but still needs shareholder and regulatory approval. Trading at roughly book value and a mid-single-digit earnings multiple, the stock already reflects much of this risk. We rate it a Hold: not attractive enough to add given the asset-quality and concentration caveats, but not overvalued or deteriorating enough to call a Sell.
